CPP-32 is activated during neuronal cell death in animal models of ischemia and epilepsy, respectively.

the CPP-32 proteolytic activity in hippocampal homogenates is increased following ischemic insults, that the increase is detectable before cell death, and that the activation of CPP-32 is correlated with neuronal apoptosis in vivo.

elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal apoptosis and the role of CPP-32 in ischemic and epileptogenic brain damage.
the role of apoptosis in the selective vulnerability of the hippocampus.
the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal death in cerebral ischemia and epileptic seizures.

CPP32 is a protease that is upregulated in the brain after cerebral ischemia and is involved in neuronal death in the hippocampus.
CPP-32 may be involved in neuronal apoptosis in vivo and in vitro.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of CPP- 32, a member of the ICE family of proteases, is significantly up-regulated in CA1 hippocampus neurons after ischemia, and in CA3/CA1 hippocampus neurons following kainate-mediated epileptiform activity.
the expression of CPP- 32, an ICE related protease, was increased in hippocampal pyrimidal neurons following ischemia induced by global cardiac arrest and kainate-mediated seizures.

the activation of CPP-32 may be an important step in the process of neuronal cell death following cerebral ischemia and that the activation of the CPP-32 proteolytic activity may be a potential target for the development of novel neuroprotective drugs.
